The letter coordinate j=7*octave+letter_index and absolute number transform independently as j+d+7o,m+c+12o. From C4=60, chromatic+1 with diatonic0 gives C#4; diatonic+1 gives Db4. Both61 preserve different spellings; semitone offset alone underdetermines the letter.

B3 plus one letter/semitone gives C4=60; C4 down one letter/two semitones gives Bb3=58. B#3=60 and Cb4=59 cross the natural C boundary. Letter, alteration and written octave jointly determine the sounding number.

Octave change-1 with zero d/c changes j by-7 and m by-12, giving C3=48. C4 with alteration-12 reaches the number but not the intended representation. Integer storage/commented ranges alone do not validate accidental support.

C#4/Db4 plus one letter/two semitones become D#4/Eb4, both63. Keeping target spelling and declared offsets supports the demonstrated exact inverse; keeping only63 loses the two origins. The ten fixed cases are bounded arithmetic, not a general notation implementation.

Actual MusicXML type retains Step/Alter/Octave and computes an integer projection; selected parser attributes omit transpose. CapoSkill sharp/flat preference is distinct from diatonic spelling transformation. A typed transform with explicit supported context and independent enharmonic/boundary/inverse checks precedes any DSL proposal; no native adapter, score import/render or playback was delivered.
